topics.name: Wishes: I wish I were / wish + could
Simple present for habits and agreement
Time clauses (when, as soon as, until, just as)

options: I wish I were a hawker.
I wish I am a hawker.
I wish I be a hawker.
questions.rule: For a wish about the present that is not true, use were: I wish I were ...

options: The gardener digs the ground every afternoon.
The gardener dig the ground every afternoon.
The gardener digging the ground every afternoon.
questions.rule: A habit with a singular subject takes verb + -s: The gardener digs.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct prepositions.
options: I come back from school on four in the afternoon.
I come back from school at four on the afternoon.
I come back from school at four in the afternoon.
questions.rule: Use at for clock time and in for parts of the day: at four in the afternoon.

options: When the bell will ring, we go out to play.
When the bell rings, we go out to play.
When the bell ring, we go out to play.
questions.rule: In a when clause about habits, use the simple present: When the bell rings.

options: Nobody take the gardener to task.
Nobody are taking the gardener to task.
Nobody takes the gardener to task.
questions.rule: Nobody is singular, so the verb takes -s: Nobody takes.

options: Ravi wishes he can stay out in the rain.
Ravi wish he could stay out in the rain.
Ravi wishes he could stay out in the rain.
questions.rule: After wish, can moves back to could; Ravi takes wishes.

options: Just as it was getting dark, my mother send me to bed.
Just as it was getting dark, my mother sent me to bed.
Just as it getting dark, my mother sent me to bed.
questions.rule: Past continuous needs was getting; the main action is simple past: sent.

options: If I were a watchman, I will walk the street all night.
If I am a watchman, I would walk the street all night.
If I were a watchman, I would walk the street all night.
questions.rule: An imagined situation: If I were ..., I would ...

questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (for five years) and since with a starting point (since 2020).

questions.rule: A when clause about the future uses the simple present: when I walk.
A wish for an ability you don't have uses could: wishes she could fly.
The fixed phrase is go to bed.
Look! and right now show an action happening now: present continuous is coming.

questions.before: I will not go to bed
questions.after: the watchman has passed our window.
questions.rule: Until joins a clause and means 'up to the time when'; by and during need a noun.
wish + subject + were expresses an unreal wish.
Frequency words like never come before the main verb: never hurries.
Up and down + place shows movement to and fro.
As soon as + clause, then the main clause.
wishes he could + base verb expresses a wish for something not possible now.
He takes verb + -s in the simple present: He sells.

chat: When do you leave for school?
options: I leave at ten in the morning.
I leave on ten in the morning.
I leave at ten on the morning.
questions.rule: at + clock time, in + the morning.

chat: Do you like being a student?
options: Yes, but sometimes I wish I am a gardener.
Yes, but sometimes I wish I were a gardener.
Yes, but sometimes I wishes I were a gardener.
questions.rule: I wish (no -s with I) + I were for an unreal wish.

chat: Will you call me when you reach school?
options: Yes, I will call you when I reach.
Yes, I will call you when I will reach.
Yes, I call you when I reached.
questions.rule: Future in the main clause, simple present in the when clause: will call ... when I reach.

chat: Does your gardener work on Sundays?
options: No, he doesn't work on Sundays.
No, he don't work on Sundays.
No, he doesn't works on Sundays.
questions.rule: He doesn't + base verb: doesn't work.

chat: How long have you lived in this lane?
questions.rule: Present perfect + since + starting point: have lived here since 2019.

chat: Why do you watch your paper boats so closely?
options: I wish they can float all the way to a faraway land.
I wish they could floated all the way to a faraway land.
I wish they could float all the way to a faraway land.
questions.rule: After wish, use could + base verb: could float.

chat: Go to bed now. It's very late.
options: I'll go as soon as I will finish this page.
I'll go as soon as I finished this page.
I'll go as soon as I finish this page.
questions.rule: After as soon as, use the simple present for a future action: as soon as I finish.

options: I wish I were a gardener.
I wish I am a gardener.
I wish I were not a gardener.
questions.rule: The wish is the opposite of the fact, with were: I wish I were a gardener.

questions.source: The watchman goes to bed early.
options: The watchman does not goes to bed early.
The watchman does not go to bed early.
The watchman do not go to bed early.
questions.rule: Singular subject: does not + base verb go.

questions.source: The gong sounds ten. I walk to school.
options: When the gong sounds ten, I walk to school.
When the gong will sound ten, I walk to school.
When the gong sound ten, I walk to school.
questions.rule: Keep the simple present in both parts: When the gong sounds ten, I walk ...

questions.source: The gardener waters the roses every afternoon.
options: Does the gardener waters the roses every afternoon?
Does the gardener water the roses every afternoon?
Do the gardener water the roses every afternoon?
questions.rule: Singular subject: Does + subject + base verb: Does the gardener water ...?

questions.source: It gets dark. My mother sends me to bed.
options: As soon as it will get dark, my mother sends me to bed.
As soon as it gets dark, my mother send me to bed.
As soon as it gets dark, my mother sends me to bed.
questions.rule: Simple present in both clauses; my mother takes sends.

questions.source: I cannot stay out in the rain.
options: I wish I could stay out in the rain.
I wish I can stay out in the rain.
I wish I could not stay out in the rain.
questions.rule: cannot (fact) becomes the wish I wish I could ...

options: He is not took to task by anybody.
He was not taken to task by anybody.
He is not taken to task by anybody.
questions.rule: Simple present passive: is + past participle taken; nobody becomes not ... by anybody.

questions.source: As soon as the watchman lit his lantern, the street became bright.
options: No sooner had the watchman lit his lantern than the street became bright.
No sooner did the watchman lit his lantern than the street became bright.
No sooner had the watchman lit his lantern when the street became bright.
questions.rule: No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than ...
